title: Breaking a Teen into Ten and Some

steps.body: Building runs backwards too: any teen BREAKS into its ten and its ones. Sixteen splits into 10 and 6, always.
steps.narration: Building runs backwards too: any teen BREAKS into its ten and its ones. Sixteen splits into 10 and 6, always.

widget.prompt: A full group of 10 is already shown. Add the extra dots needed to make 16.

commonCounts.feedback: 0 leaves 6 dots still missing — the ten alone only makes 10, not 16.
5 leaves 1 dot still missing; ten and 5 is 15, one short of 16.
7 adds 1 too many; ten and 7 is 17, one past 16.

widget.missFeedback: The ten is done; count on from 10 while adding dots, and stop when you reach 16.
widget.successFeedback: 16 built — one complete ten and 6 more, exactly what the teen numeral says.

predict.reveal: The numeral stores the split: one ten on the left, six ones on the right.

cml.actionGoal: Build one complete ten, then count on the ones, for knb decompose teen.
invariants: Every teen number is one complete ten and some ones — the left digit records the finished ten, the right digit counts the extras — and that split is what knb decompose teen rests on.
misconceptions: Reading the 1 of a teen as “one” instead of one TEN, or counting only the leftover ones and forgetting the completed ten.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more dot joined the ones, which teen would the frame show then?

widget.prompt: Which pair is NOT a split of 18?

options.label: 10 and 8
options.feedback: 10 + 8 = 18, so this pair is a valid split of 18 — the teen split itself.

options.label: 18 and 0
options.feedback: 18 + 0 = 18, so this pair is a valid split of 18, keeping everything in one part.

options.label: 17 and 1
options.feedback: 17 + 1 = 18, so this pair is a valid split of 18.

options.label: 10 and 9
options.feedback: Correct — 10 + 9 = 19, one too many, so this pair is not a split of 18.

widget.prompt: Reverse the build: show the seven leftover ones after a group of 17 fills one ten-frame.

commonCounts.feedback: That shows one too few loose ones. The target needs 7.
That shows one too many loose ones. Stop at 7.

widget.missFeedback: Keep the full ten fixed and build exactly 7 loose ones.
widget.successFeedback: 17 is one complete ten and 7 more.

widget.prompt: 17 dots fill one ten-frame with some left outside. How many are left over?

options.label: 17 — all of them are left over
options.feedback: Ten of the seventeen sit INSIDE the frame; only the ones beyond the ten remain out.

options.label: 7 — the ten is inside, the rest ride outside
options.feedback: Correct — 17 is one full ten and 7 ones, so exactly 7 dots cannot fit in the frame.

options.label: 10 — the frame's worth
options.feedback: The frame's ten is the part that fits; the leftovers are what exceeds it.

options.label: 1 — just one dot
options.feedback: One would make eleven in all; seventeen carries seven past the completed ten.

widget.prompt: What number comes right before 17? Hop one back and tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 17 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop back to reach 16.
15 goes one complete hop too far. Count exactly 1 hop back from 17 to reach 16.

widget.missFeedback: Count 1 back from 17: you land on 16.
widget.successFeedback: 16 — one hop back through the teens, one less than 17.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — one hop back from 17 reaches 16.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right before 17 means a single hop back, stopping on 16.

options.feedback: 10 + 5 = 15, so this pair is a valid split of 15 — the teen split itself.

options.label: 10 and 6
options.feedback: Correct — 10 + 6 = 16, one too many, so this pair is not a split of 15.

Adding the parts re-makes the whole.
